32:- **Runner tf-lite-6 (2026-10-12, branch `feature/cyrus-mc-testing-weapons`, not merged).** (1) **Survival combat stress bot**: vanilla mob AI ignores creative players (verified in Paper 1.21.11 bytecode: `MeleeAttackGoal` checks `isCreative`/`isSpectator`, `TargetingConditions` use `canBeSeenAsEnemy`), so a creative bot was a false green for mobs and bosses. `stress.botMode` = `build` (creative block stress, default) or `combat` (survival: gamemode reply checked, difficulty easy, sword + food + resistance over RCON, capped waves of daylight-safe husks/spiders tagged `nxstress`, it fights the nearest foe; hits, damage taken, kills, deaths recorded). The gate picks it from the build's planned lanes (`creature`, `designBoss`) or the designer bosses flag (`stressBotModeFor`). Real: 40 hits, 9 kills, 20 TPS. (2) **Worldgen density probes** (`worldgen` check, `lib/cyrus/testflight/worldgen.ts` + `lib.js`): force-load 3x3 chunks per sample in the pack's own dimension, wait with `execute if loaded`, count with `execute in <dim> run fill <16 x <=64 x 16> minecraft:air replace <block>` (reply strings from the jars' en_us.json), judge against a stated coarse range derived from the data pack spec (max = attempts x 8 x size x chunks x 2; min 1 only when the spec promises ore in the box); the failure names the feature with measured vs expected. Destructive only in the throwaway world; a timed-out fill is never retried. Gate switch `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_WORLDGEN` (default OFF), stored as `StoredFlight.worldgen`, never blocks Install. (3) **Prove the harness can fail** (`lib/cyrus/testflight/mutants.ts`, `test/cyrus-mc-mutants-real.ts`): a plugin that throws on enable, a plugin that spins the main thread 90 ms per tick (fixture `mainthread-spam`) and a pack with its ore moved into the air must each be REJECTED by the right check with the cause named, and each good control must pass. It found a real gap: a mod that lags from the moment it enables was judged "slow host, not run"; the stress judge now samples the JVM CPU and fails a slow baseline that burns >= 85% of a core (`busyCpuPct`), keeping not_run for a starved host.
40:5. **Emitters audit** (`lib/cyrus/safety/perf-caps.ts`, test-pinned): designers, motion, data packs and worldgen already had per-activation / plugin-wide caps; added for data pack tick functions: unconditional summon refused, particles <= 64 per command (1000 anywhere), fill/clone <= 64 blocks, unfiltered `execute as @e` warned. Owner decision: a cooldown-0 designer click ability has no per-player floor (adding one changes every existing designer jar). Weapon components (2026-10-12) are audited as their own emitter: rays and line-of-sight checks spend the action budget, a click weapon needs cooldownTicks >= 4, beams have no timer and at most 16 live.
71:- **Weapon components (2026-10-12, branch `feature/cyrus-mc-testing-weapons`, not merged)**: three item-designer actions with their own component `designer/Weapons.java` (`lib/cyrus/designer/components/weapons.ts`), added only to mods that use them so every existing designer jar stays byte-identical. `hitscan` (range 1-64, damage per pellet, pellets 1-12, spread 0-15 degrees on a fixed sunflower pattern, rays stop at the first block, pellet damage SUMMED per target and dealt once after `setNoDamageTicks(0)`, optional tracer particle and per-target actions); `beam` (range 1-32, pulses every 2-20 ticks for 10-100 ticks, follows the aim, the first entity on the ray takes each pulse, one beam per player, at most 16 live, ends when the item leaves the hand, no timer: a chain of single delayed steps behind the re-entry guard); `area_blast` (radius 1-8, linear falloff to 0 at the edge, players take `playerScale` (default 0.5), never the user, at most 16 targets, line of sight, optional knockback; no explosion and no block change). Lag-bomb proof: every ray spends one action of the 64-action budget, hits spend entities (32), particles come from the 512 budget; a click-triggered weapon needs `cooldownTicks >= 4` (or charges). **Full-auto is not possible server-side**: the client repeats a held right-click only every 4 ticks and sends no held state; real full-auto belongs to the client-mod lane. Real: javac 0 warnings and strict scan clean on 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 1.21.11 / 26.2; the playtest bot on Paper 1.21.11 measured the mechanics exactly (hitscan 4 -> pig 6.0; four summed 1-damage pellets -> 6.0, then 2.0 five ticks later; blast 6 -> target 4.0, a pig 2 blocks from the centre 7.0, the user 20.0; beam 10 x 0.5 -> 5.0).
52:- **D-56, 2026-10-12 (agent working default, owner to confirm). Designer weapons fire at most every 4 ticks.** A hitscan / beam / area_blast on a click trigger needs `cooldownTicks >= 4` or charges (validator code `weapon_cooldown`). Rule: every game ships ONE capability catalogue (every lane x every supported version, reason, substitute, minVersion)
and the planner warns from it before credits are spent; no game leaves maturity `planned` without it.
Playbook change: phase 2 step 6 + exit criterion (1.1.0).

### L8 A green test proves nothing until the same harness turns red (Minecraft, 2026-10-12)
Two Test Flight results were green for the wrong reason. The stress bot played in creative, and vanilla mob AI ignores
creative players (Paper 1.21.11 bytecode: MeleeAttackGoal checks isCreative/isSpectator), so every mob / boss stress test
was a false green. And a plugin that lagged from the moment it enabled was judged "slow host, not run", never a fail.
Both were found only by flying one-defect mutants (throws on enable, spins the main thread, ore placed in air) next to
their good controls.
Rule: every new check ships with at least one mutant it must reject with the cause named, plus a control that passes;
a bot that tests combat runs in survival. A server-side probe beats "it loads" (worldgen: count the ore, do not just boot).
Playbook change: phase 5 (verification) gains the mutant + control pair as an exit criterion.

### L9 Second-hand engine notes are hypotheses, check them against this platform's bytecode (Minecraft, 2026-10-12)
The universal-modder field notes (Fabric / Forge) said a height query on an unloaded chunk returns the world bottom. On
Paper it does the opposite: `CraftWorld.getHighestBlockYAt` calls `ServerLevel.getChunk`, a synchronous load/generate on
the main thread (javap -c on 1.21.1 .. 26.2). The trap is real on Paper, but it is a lag spike, not a wrong height.
Rule: a fact from another loader or another game is V-s until javap (API) or javap -c (implementation) on the exact jars
confirms it; encode only the verified half, mark the rest second hand.
Playbook change: phase 3 (research) step "verify every borrowed fact on the target jars".

### L10 Say what the platform cannot do before it is built (Minecraft weapons, 2026-10-12)
A server plugin cannot do full-auto: the client repeats a held right-click only every 4 ticks and sends no "button held"
state. The weapon components therefore refuse a click weapon without cooldownTicks >= 4, the prompt and README say so,
and real full-auto is filed under the client-mod lane.
Rule: a capability limit found while building becomes a validator code, a prompt line and a customer-facing note in the
same change.
Playbook change: none (follows L7).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
